# Negative-instruction backfire in style prompts — concept pack

- **self**: Negative-instruction backfire in style prompts (7/3)

## Structure and components

- [statement] In a 40,000-sample study of forbidden-word constraints, 87.5% of violations were 'priming failures' (naming the word activated it) and 12.5% were 'override failures' from late-layer feed-forward networks; violation probability follows a logistic curve in the model's intrinsic probability of the forbidden token. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08070 · keywords: Negative-instruction backfire in style prompts

## How it works

- [statement] Mentioning a topic in the prompt makes the model more likely to mention it even when told to avoid it (the Pink Elephant problem); prompting alone was outperformed by a Llama-2-13B model fine-tuned with Direct Principle Feedback, which matched GPT-4 on the authors' test set. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07896 · keywords: Negative-instruction backfire in style prompts · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12381

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Listing banned words in a style prompt is an antipattern: the list itself places the tokens in context and primes them; pair any unavoidable prohibition with a named replacement. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08070 · keywords: Negative-instruction backfire in style prompts · also: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Circuit analysis suggests sparse middle-layer attention heads amplify forbidden tokens while early layers suppress them, so ironic rebound reflects competing internal representations rather than simple suppression. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12381 · keywords: Negative-instruction backfire in style prompts
- [statement] Anthropic's prompting docs advise telling Claude what to do instead of what not to do (e.g. replace 'Do not use markdown' with a positive description of the wanted prose format). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices · keywords: Negative-instruction backfire in style prompts · also: https://mavka.ai/blog/negative-vs-positive-instructions
- [statement] The backfire is scoped, not universal: a small code-review test found prohibitions matched the positive reframe on discrete actions and underperformed only on judgment calls (2/3 false positives with prohibition vs 0/3 with reframe); earlier inverse-scaling evidence came from classification tasks on older models. (low confidence) — https://mavka.ai/blog/negative-vs-positive-instructions · keywords: Negative-instruction backfire in style prompts

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Negation instructions such as 'do not mention X' can paradoxically increase the accessibility of X in LLMs (ironic rebound); rebound appears immediately after negation and worsens with longer or semantic distractor text, while repetition supports suppression. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12381 · keywords: Negative-instruction backfire in style prompts · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08070
